_note: DRAFT starter goal bank for GABAY. Proposed by the development team and NOT yet agreed with the SNED Coordinator. Loaded with status 'draft'; the Coordinator reviews, edits and activates goals in the Goal bank screen. Domain codes match the extraction FindingDomain values.

domains.name: Behavior and social skills
domains.description: Classroom behavior, self-regulation and social interaction.

domains.name: Self-help and daily living
domains.description: Independence in personal care and daily routines.

domains.name: Other
domains.description: Goals that do not fit another domain.

goals.statement: Given a spoken one-syllable word, the learner will say the first sound of the word with 80% accuracy in 3 consecutive weekly probes.
Given 10 spoken CVC words, the learner will blend the individual sounds into a word with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
Given flash cards of all 26 letters, the learner will say the sound of each letter with 90% accuracy in 2 consecutive probes.
Given a list of 20 CVC words, the learner will decode and read the words aloud independently with 80% accuracy in 3 consecutive probes.
Given a list of 20 two-syllable words, the learner will decode and read the words aloud with 80% accuracy in 3 consecutive probes.
Given a decodable text at the learner's instructional level, the learner will read the text aloud with 85% word accuracy across 3 sessions.
Given an unfamiliar Grade 1 reading passage, the learner will read aloud at 40 words correct per minute on 3 of 4 weekly probes.
Given an unfamiliar Grade 3 reading passage, the learner will read aloud at 70 words correct per minute on 3 of 4 weekly probes.
Given 10 picture cards of common classroom and home words, the learner will name the pictured word in English or Filipino with 80% accuracy in 3 consecutive sessions.
After listening to or reading a short story, the learner will retell the main character, setting and one event in 4 of 5 trials.
After reading a short passage at instructional level, the learner will answer literal who, what and where questions with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
After reading a short passage at instructional level, the learner will answer inferential why and how questions with 70% accuracy across 4 sessions.
Given a model, the learner will copy 10 upper- and lowercase letters with correct formation and within the lines with 80% accuracy in 3 consecutive sessions.
The learner will write his or her first and last name legibly without a model in 4 of 5 trials.
Given 10 dictated CVC words, the learner will spell the words correctly with 80% accuracy on 3 consecutive weekly tests.
Given a picture prompt, the learner will write a complete sentence with a capital letter and end punctuation, scoring level 3 on the class writing rubric on 3 of 4 samples.
Given a set of up to 20 objects, the learner will count the objects and say the total with 90% accuracy in 3 consecutive sessions.
The learner will read and write numbers from 1 to 100 with 90% accuracy in 2 consecutive probes.
Given counters or other manipulatives, the learner will solve 10 single-digit addition problems with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
Given counters or other manipulatives, the learner will solve 10 single-digit subtraction problems with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
Given 10 two-digit addition and subtraction problems with regrouping, the learner will solve them with 80% accuracy on 3 consecutive weekly probes.
Given a one-step addition or subtraction word problem read aloud, the learner will choose the operation and solve it using drawings or objects in 4 of 5 trials.
Given Philippine coins and bills up to 100 pesos, the learner will identify each and count a given amount with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
Given an analog clock, the learner will tell time to the hour and half hour with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
During independent seatwork, the learner will remain on task for 10 consecutive minutes with no more than one teacher prompt in 4 of 5 observed sessions.
Using a visual timer and scheduled short breaks, the learner will be on task during 80% of observed intervals in seatwork over 2 weeks.
Given a two-step classroom direction, the learner will complete both steps within 1 minute without additional prompts in 4 of 5 opportunities.
Given a three-step classroom direction, the learner will complete all steps in order without additional prompts in 4 of 5 opportunities.
Using a visual schedule and a one-minute warning, the learner will move to the next activity within 2 minutes without upset in 80% of transitions over 2 weeks.
When told about an unexpected change in the daily routine, the learner will use a taught calming strategy and accept the change in 4 of 5 occasions.

goals.criterion: per recess period on 4 of 5 days
goals.statement: During recess or group work, the learner will start a positive interaction with a peer (greeting, asking to play, sharing) at least 3 times per period on 4 of 5 days.
During a structured game with peers, the learner will wait for his or her turn and take turns appropriately in 4 of 5 opportunities.
When upset or frustrated, the learner will ask for a break or use a taught calming strategy instead of leaving the area or crying in 4 of 5 observed occasions.

goals.criterion: or fewer per day for 3 consecutive weeks
goals.statement: The learner will reduce calling out without raising a hand to 2 or fewer times per day for 3 consecutive weeks.
Given a picture or classroom event, the learner will describe it using a complete sentence of at least 5 words in 4 of 5 opportunities.
When needing help or an item, the learner will make a request using a full phrase (e.g. 'Please help me') in 80% of opportunities across 3 sessions.
Given simple who, what and where questions in English or Filipino, the learner will answer with a relevant response with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
When asked a question, the learner will answer it directly without first repeating (echoing) the question in 4 of 5 trials.
In a structured conversation with a peer, the learner will keep the conversation going for at least 3 turns on the same topic in 3 of 4 opportunities.
During writing tasks, the learner will hold a pencil with a functional tripod grasp, with no more than one reminder, in 4 of 5 observed tasks.
Given a printed shape or line, the learner will cut along it with scissors staying within a quarter inch of the line for 80% of its length across 3 sessions.
Given a model, the learner will trace and then copy basic shapes (circle, square, triangle) recognisably in 4 of 5 trials.
The learner will catch a playground ball thrown from 2 meters with both hands in 4 of 5 trials.

goals.criterion: of checklist steps on 4 of 5 days
goals.statement: The learner will put on and button a uniform shirt independently, completing 100% of the checklist steps on 4 of 5 days.
Using a picture sequence, the learner will wash and dry hands after toileting and before eating, completing 90% of the steps independently on 4 of 5 days.
During snack time, the learner will open his or her own food containers and eat using a spoon or fork independently on 4 of 5 days.
During a teacher-led group lesson, the learner will look at the speaker or materials and respond when called on for 5 consecutive minutes in 4 of 5 sessions.
Given a sequence of 4 pictures shown for 10 seconds, the learner will recall and arrange them in the correct order in 4 of 5 trials.
When faced with a simple everyday problem (e.g. a missing material), the learner will name one possible solution and try it before asking for help in 3 of 4 opportunities.
Given a set of 10 objects or pictures, the learner will sort them by one attribute (colour, shape or category) with 80% accuracy across 3 sessions.
